purpose: Smallest useful real-host vertical slice for the pinned Mozc x64 TIP. It proves TSF activation, composition preedit, candidate presentation, and commit; it is not the complete release test matrix.

application.requirement: A visible, editable, non-secure desktop text control in an x64 Windows process.

preconditions: Run the exact DLL that the harness hashed in an x64 PowerShell process.
Use the 64-bit Windows TSF registry view and the pinned upstream Mozc profile.
Start from a new untitled document with no existing text or selection.
Do not use a password, secure-desktop, elevated, or restricted-token field for this minimal slice.

steps.action: Focus the text control and activate the pinned Mozc Japanese profile with the normal Windows language/profile UI or shortcut.
steps.expected: Mozc Japanese input is active; no KanaAI identity is claimed.

steps.action: Type the ASCII letters kana without pressing Space.
steps.evidence: The three-character reading is visible as inline preedit, and the document has not committed Latin text.
A candidate window is visible and its primary candidate is 変換.
The document contains 変換, the reading preedit and candidate window are gone, and focus remains in the text control.

steps.action: Close the document without saving and confirm the host process exits cleanly.
steps.evidence: No crash dialog, stale candidate window, or orphan Mozc process remains.

notCovered: performance, learning, broker, or AI quality
failureGuidance: If the profile cannot be activated, report registration-live failure and do not treat DLL load as TSF proof.
If preedit is absent, report host failure and retain the exact profile/app/artifact evidence.
If candidates are absent, verify mozc_server.exe and the complete runtime before retrying.
If commit differs, report the observed text verbatim; do not normalize it to the expected value.
